quizzes.title: India's Gender Gap Profile
quizzes.passage: The Global Gender Gap Index is an annual flagship publication of the World Economic Forum. It tracks the extent to which countries have closed gender disparities, rather than simply measuring women's absolute outcomes. The index has four dimensions: economic participation and opportunity, educational attainment, health and survival, and political empowerment. Each nation is scored from 0 to 1, and the scores are expressed on a 0-100 scale, where 100 represents complete parity. In the 2026 report, India retained its position in the rankings. Its performance is uneven across the dimensions. In educational attainment and in health and survival, India's scores are close to complete parity, and the booklet describes near-complete parity between boys and girls in secondary and tertiary enrolment. Economic participation and political empowerment show far wider gaps. Women are a small share of ministers and of members of the Lok Sabha, and they hold a limited share of senior leadership and managerial posts. In corporate India, women are also few among chief executives and board members. The booklet notes that progress in education and health has not yet carried over to the economic and political dimensions. The booklet also notes that women's share among professional and technical workers has increased, even as women remain under-represented in senior roles. Overall, the booklet presents India's gender gap as a mix of strong and weak dimensions.

questions.q: According to the 2026 report, what share of ministers in India are women?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that women are 5.9% of ministers, compared with a peak of 30% in 2019.

questions.q: What was the peak share of women ministers in India, according to the booklet?
questions.explanation: The booklet says women's share of ministers peaked at 30% in 2019.

questions.q: What share of the 18th Lok Sabha elected in 2024 was women?
questions.explanation: The booklet gives women as 13.6% (74) of the 18th Lok Sabha in 2024.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): India's score in economic participation and opportunity is lower than its score in educational attainment.
Reason (R): The index is expressed on a 0-100 scale, where 100 represents complete parity.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are supported by the booklet, but the 0-100 scale does not explain why the economic score is lower.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Educational attainment   ->   A. 24.5%
II. Health and survival   ->   B. 96.6%
III. Economic participation and opportunity   ->   C. 95.6%
IV. Political empowerment   ->   D. 41.2%
questions.explanation: The booklet gives India's scores as 96.6% for education, 95.6% for health, 41.2% for economic participation and 24.5% for political empowerment.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Women are 17% of CEOs in Indian corporates.
II. Women are 20% of board members in Indian corporates.
III. Women are 30% of ministers in India in 2026.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the booklet, while III gives the 2019 peak rather than the 2026 share of 5.9%.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements about India's performance are correct?
I. India's score in educational attainment is 96.6%.
II. Women hold 24.5% of senior leadership and managerial positions in India.
III. Women hold 13.1% of senior leadership and managerial positions in India.
questions.explanation: Statements I and III match the booklet, while II wrongly uses the 24.5% political empowerment score for senior leadership.

quizzes.title: India's Dimension Scores
quizzes.passage: India's overall gender parity score in the 2026 report is 64.5%, and the booklet compares it with a global average. The country's performance differs sharply across the four dimensions. Education is its strongest area, and the booklet says India has attained near-complete parity between boys and girls in secondary and tertiary enrolment. Health and survival is also close to parity. Economic participation and political empowerment are much weaker. Women's share among professional and technical workers has nearly doubled since 2006, which shows some progress in the workforce. However, few women reach the top. The booklet notes low representation in leadership, with few women among chief executives and board members in Indian corporates. In the political sphere, women hold a small share of seats in the Lok Sabha, and their share of ministers has fallen from an earlier peak. Among the booklet's figures for the workforce, women hold a notable share of professional roles, but few hold the most senior positions. Women are also underrepresented in senior leadership and managerial positions. The booklet notes that gains in education and health have not yet translated into the economic and political dimensions. In the Lok Sabha, women's share in 2024 is below their share in 2019. The overall picture is one of progress in some areas and persistent gaps in others.

questions.q: What per cent of board members in Indian corporates are women?
questions.explanation: The booklet says women are 20% of board members in Indian corporates.

questions.q: What per cent of CEOs in Indian corporates are women?
questions.explanation: The booklet says only 17% of CEOs in Indian corporates are women.

questions.q: What is India's score in economic participation and opportunity, in per cent?
questions.explanation: The booklet records India's economic participation and opportunity score as 41.2%.

questions.q: What is India's score in health and survival, in per cent?
questions.explanation: The booklet records India's health and survival score as 95.6%.

questions.q: What per cent of professional and technical workers in India are women, according to the booklet?
questions.explanation: The booklet says women's share among professional and technical workers has increased to 49.9%.

questions.q: What was women's share in the Lok Sabha in 2019, in per cent?
questions.explanation: The booklet says women were 14.4% of the Lok Sabha in 2019, down to 13.6% in 2024.

questions.q: What is India's score in political empowerment, in per cent?
questions.explanation: The booklet records India's political empowerment score as 24.5%.

quizzes.title: Barriers Facing Women and Girls
quizzes.passage: Women's participation in India's labour market has risen between 2017-18 and 2023-24, but much of their work remains in informal, low-paid roles. Workplace safety concerns and inadequate childcare are among the major hurdles they face. Women also carry a heavy load of unpaid domestic work, and the booklet puts a value on this work in economic terms. Girls' education faces obstacles too. A considerable share of girls aged 15 to 18 are not in school, and many drop out because of a lack of hygiene infrastructure and societal stigma. Female literacy also trails male literacy. Government programmes respond to these gaps by supporting girls' education, maternal health and women's access to financial services. Maternal health programmes have contributed to a fall in maternal mortality, and the National Health Mission aims to deliver affordable, quality healthcare to India's most vulnerable. The booklet also notes that many government programmes face setbacks due to poor outreach, lack of awareness and weak execution, especially in remote and rural areas. Constitutional provisions also address women's representation in legislatures. The booklet lists these challenges in its section on barriers to gender equality in India. In the education system, female literacy is set against male literacy as one of the gaps the booklet highlights. The booklet describes participation as rising despite most women remaining in informal, low-paid roles.

questions.q: What was female labour participation in India in 2017-18, according to the booklet?
questions.explanation: The booklet says female labour participation grew from 23.3% in 2017-18 to 41.7% in 2023-24.

questions.q: Maternal health programmes have cut the maternal mortality rate to what level, according to the booklet?
questions.explanation: The booklet says maternal health programmes cut the maternal mortality rate from 174 to 97.

questions.q: The Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam is which Constitutional Amendment Act?
questions.explanation: The booklet names it as the 106th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2023.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Most women in India are in formal, high-paid jobs.
Reason (R): Most women in India are in informal, low-paid roles despite rising participation.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The booklet says most women are in informal, low-paid roles, so A is false while R is true.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Beti Bachao Beti Padhao   ->   B. Financial access for women
II. Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana   ->   D. Schoolgirls in STEM fields
III. Pradhan Mantri Jan-Dhan Yojana   ->   A. Maternity benefits for pregnant and lactating women
IV. Vigyan Jyoti   ->   C. Falling child sex ratio
questions.explanation: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao targets the falling child sex ratio, PM Matru Vandana Yojana offers maternity benefits, Jan-Dhan supports financial access and Vigyan Jyoti empowers schoolgirls in STEM.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Over 28 crore women have Jan Dhan bank accounts.
II. The Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam mandates 50% representation for women in legislatures.
III. Female labour participation grew from 23.3% (2017-18) to 41.7% (2023-24).
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement II is wrong because the mandate is 33%, while I and III match the booklet.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. Unpaid household work is valued at 7.5% of GDP.
II. Most girls aged 15 to 18 are not in school.
III. PM Matru Vandana Yojana was launched in 2017.
questions.explanation: Statements I and III match the booklet, while II is wrong because 40% of girls aged 15 to 18 are not in school.

quizzes.title: Government Schemes for Women and Girls
quizzes.passage: Several programmes aim to improve outcomes for girls and women. Beti Bachao Beti Padhao targets the falling child sex ratio and champions girls' survival, safety and schooling. Vigyan Jyoti is a flagship scheme that empowers meritorious schoolgirls to shine in STEM fields. Pradhan Mantri Jan-Dhan Yojana supports women's autonomy through financial access, and women have opened large numbers of bank accounts under it. The National Health Mission aims to deliver affordable, quality healthcare to India's most vulnerable. Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana offers maternity benefits to pregnant and lactating women across India. Maternal health programmes have reduced the maternal mortality rate. Unpaid work is another part of the picture. Women spend many hours each day on household chores, and the booklet estimates the economic value of this unpaid work in lakh crore. Female literacy remains lower than male literacy, and a large share of girls in the 15 to 18 age group are outside school. Despite rising participation, most women remain in informal, low-paid work. Workplace safety concerns and inadequate childcare remain major hurdles for women at work. The Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam mandates representation for women in legislatures. The booklet also notes that many government programmes face setbacks due to poor outreach and weak execution, especially in remote and rural areas.

questions.q: What is the estimated economic value of women's unpaid domestic work, in lakh crore?
questions.explanation: The booklet values unpaid work at 22.7 lakh crore, or 7.5% of GDP.

questions.q: What per cent of girls aged 15 to 18 are not in school?
questions.explanation: The booklet says 40% of girls aged 15 to 18 are not in school.

questions.q: How many crore women have Jan Dhan bank accounts?
questions.explanation: The booklet says over 28 crore women have Jan Dhan bank accounts.

questions.q: From what level did the maternal mortality rate fall to 97?
questions.explanation: The booklet says maternal health programmes cut the maternal mortality rate from 174 to 97.

questions.q: In which year was the National Health Mission introduced?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists the National Health Mission as launched in 2013.

questions.q: Which department runs the Vigyan Jyoti scheme?
questions.explanation: The booklet describes Vigyan Jyoti as the Department of Science & Technology's flagship scheme.

questions.q: What per cent is female literacy in India, according to the booklet?
questions.explanation: The booklet says female literacy stands at 65%, trailing male literacy at 82%.
